_readme: Our own wording, no API needed. Edit freely. {placeholders} are filled with engine numbers. Lists = variants; each card picks one variant deterministically. Run `python -m pytest tests/test_llm.py` after editing: every variant must pass the validator (no invented numbers, status wording kept, 'projected' for yearly values, no blame, '-like' appliances).

PLAUSIBLE.unknown: a possible heating opportunity that needs confirmation

status_phrase.REPAIRED: repaired, waiting for new data to measure the saving
status_phrase.VERIFIED: a measured saving after the repair
status_phrase.DISMISSED: checked by a technician with no fault found

away_usage: On while the flat is empty

body: The {appliance} shows {phrase} since {since}, about {sek} SEK measured over the last 4 weeks (projected {low}-{high} SEK per year, not a promise).
Since {since} the {appliance} shows {phrase}: about {sek} SEK measured over the last 4 weeks, projected {low}-{high} SEK per year if nothing changes.
body_shift: The {appliance} often runs in expensive hours, {phrase}. Running it later would have saved about {sek} SEK measured over the last 4 weeks, with the same energy use (projected {low}-{high} SEK per year, not a promise).

The {appliance} mostly runs when electricity is expensive, {phrase}. Starting it later would have cost about {sek} SEK less over the last 4 weeks for the same use (projected {low}-{high} SEK per year).
manager_suffix: This is an equipment question for your building manager, not something residents caused.
The building manager can look at this; it is not about how you use it.

fault_step_change: Check that the door closes properly, then report it with the button below.
peer_outlier: Check that nothing is left running on it, then report it with the button below.
heater_pattern: Check whether a portable heater is on and tell your manager if rooms feel cold.
away_usage: Switch lights and devices off when the last person leaves the flat.
Agree in the flat that whoever leaves last does a quick switch-off round.
night_baseload: Before bed, switch off chargers, screens and anything else left on standby.
_default: Have a quick look at the appliance.

action_shift: Start it at {hour} or later instead of in the evening.

finding_manager.title: {flat_id} {appliance_id}: {title}
summary: {appliance_id} ({appliance}) shows {phrase} since {since}, status {status} with detector confidence {confidence}. Measured over the last 4 weeks: {kwh} kWh and {sek} SEK; projected {sek_low}-{sek_high} SEK per year if nothing changes.

check.fault_step_change: Check door seal, thermostat setting and compressor; compare with the appliance's normal cycle.
check.peer_outlier: Inspect the appliance and its settings against the same model in other flats.
check.heater_pattern: Check radiator function and indoor temperature before treating this as resident behaviour.
check.away_usage: No technician needed; behaviour finding for residents.
check.night_baseload: No technician needed unless residents report a device they cannot switch off.
check.peak_usage: No technician needed; residents can run the appliance later.

This week in your flat: {sek} SEK of electricity

Nice work: {pillar} is your strongest area at {value} out of 100.

encouragement: Small habits add up, and every check helps the whole flat.
Keep it up: small changes together make a real difference.

summary: Your Resident Actions score is {score} (band {band}), built from use {use}, waste {waste} and timing {timing} out of 100. Your strongest area is {strongest} and the one with most room is {weakest}.
Your flat scores {score} (band {band}) on Resident Actions: use {use}, waste {waste} and timing {timing} out of 100. {Strongest} is going best, {weakest} has the most room to improve.

use: Switch off devices you are not using, such as chargers, lights and screens.
waste: Make switching things off part of leaving the flat.
timing: Run the dishwasher-like appliance late in the evening instead of during the evening peak.
